BiblicalUsage: Jeduthun was a singer of Israel, the head of a family of Levites who stood at the east end of the altar with cymbals and harps when Solomon brought up the ark. His sons sang in the temple, and his name heads three psalms, the thirty-ninth, the sixty-second, and the seventy-seventh, given to the chief musician for Jeduthun. The family sang for generations, from David's tent to the days of Nehemiah.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God gives His people singers as well as soldiers, and the house of Jeduthun sang while the kingdom rose and fell. My position is that the music of the temple is part of the worship, and the singer's name belongs in the psalms.
